text: The ongoing transfer of Americans' wealth to OPEC — roughly $700 billion a year — helps underwrite terrorists' operations and creates little incentive for repressive regimes to accept democracy, whether in the Middle East or Latin America.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It didn't have to be this way, and it must not stay this way.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our nation must have a robust energy supply because energy drives prosperity and increases opportunity for every American.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We reject the idea that America cannot overcome its energy challenges — or that high gasoline prices are okay, as long as they are phased in gradually.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We reject half-measures and believe "No, we can't" is not a viable energy policy.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Together we can build a future around domestic energy sources that are diverse, reliable, and cleaner.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We can strengthen our national security, create a pathway to growing prosperity, and preserve our environment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The American people will rise to this challenge.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must aggressively increase our nation's energy supply, in an environmentally responsible way, and do so through a comprehensive strategy that meets both short and long term needs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: No amount of wishing or hoping can suspend the laws of supply and demand.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Leading economists agree that any actions that will increase future energy supplies will lead to lower energy prices today.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Increasing our production of American made energy and reducing our excessive reliance on foreign oil will: * Bring down the high cost of gasoline and diesel fuel.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Create more jobs for American workers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Enhance our national security.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In the long run, American production should move to zero-emission sources, and our nation's fossil fuel resources are the bridge to that emissions-free future.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: If we are to have the resources we need to achieve energy independence, we simply must draw more American oil from American soil.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support accelerated exploration, drilling and development in America, from new oilfields off the nation’s coasts to onshore fields such as those in Montana, North Dakota, and Alaska.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Green River Basin in Colorado, Utah, and Wyoming offers recoverable shale oil that is ready for development, and most of it is on federal lands.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To deliver that energy to American consumers, we will expand our refining capacity.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because of environmental extremism and regulatory blockades in Washington, not a single new refinery has been built in this country in 30 years.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We will encourage refinery construction and modernization and, with sensitivity to environmental concerns, an expedited permitting process.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Any legislation to increase domestic exploration, drilling and production must minimize any protracted legal challenges that could unreasonably delay or even preclude actual production.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose any efforts that would permanently block access to the coastal plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Nuclear energy is the most reliable zero-carbon emissions source of energy that we have.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Unwarranted fear mongering with no relationship to current technologies and safeguards has prevented us from starting construction of a single nuclear power plant in 31 years.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Meanwhile, the U.S. Navy has for decades relied upon nuclear-powered vessels, and other nations have harnessed nuclear power to pro vide a major portion of their energy consumption.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: There is no reason why the United States cannot catch up and do the same.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Confident in the promise offered by science and technology, Republicans will pursue dramatic increases in the use of all forms of safe, affordable, reliable — and clean — nuclear power.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As new plants are constructed using the highest safety and operation standards, the nation’s industrial and manufacturing base will be rejuvenated.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The labor force will expand, with nearly 15,000 high quality jobs created for every new nuclear plant built — and those workers will lead the nation away from its dependence on foreign oil.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Alternate power sources must enter the mainstream.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The technology behind solar energy has improved significantly in recent years, and the commercial development of wind power promises major benefits both in costs and in environmental protection.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans support these and other alternative energy sources, including geothermal and hydropower, and anticipate technological developments that will increase their economic viability.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We therefore advocate a long-term energy tax credit equally applicable to all renewable power sources.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans support measures to modernize the nation’s electricity grid to provide American consumers and businesses with more affordable, reliable power.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We will work to unleash innovation so entrepreneurs can develop technologies for a more advanced and robust United States transmission system that meets our growing energy demands.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Although alternate fuels will shape our energy future, coal — America's most affordable and abundant energy resource and the source of most of our electricity — remains a strategic national resource that must play a major role in energy independence.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We look to innovative technology to transform America’s coal supplies into clean fuels capable of powering motor vehicles and aircraft.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support coal-to-liquid and gasification initiatives, just as we support investment in the development and deployment of carbon capture and storage technologies, which can reduce emissions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We firmly oppose efforts by Democrats to block the construction of new coal-fired power plants.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: No strategy for reducing energy costs will be viable without a commitment to continued coal production and utilization.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Natural gas is plentiful in North America, but we can extract more and do a better job of distributing it nationwide to cook our food, heat our homes, and serve as a growing option as a transportation fuel.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Both independently and in cooperation with alternative fuels, natural gas will be an essential part of any long-term energy solution.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must ensure it gets to consumers safely and quickly.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We embrace the open energy cooperation and trading relationship with our neighbors Canada and Mexico, including proven oil reserves and vast, untapped Canadian hydroelectric generation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: While we grow our supplies, we must also reduce our demand — not by changing our lifestyles but by putting the free market to work and taking advantage of technological breakthroughs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Conservation does not mean deprivation; it means efficiency and achieving more with less.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Most Americans today endeavor to conserve fossil fuels, whether in their cars or in their home heating, but we can do better.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We can construct better and smarter buildings, use smarter thermostats and transmission grids, increase recycling, and make energy-efficient consumer purchases. Wireless communications, for example, can increase telecommuting options and cut back on business travel.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Republican goal is to ensure that Americans have more conservation options that will enable them to make the best choices for their families.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must continue to develop alternative fuels, such as biofuels, especially cellulosic ethanol, and hasten their technological advances to next-generation production.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As America develops energy technology for the 21st century, policy makers must consider the burden that rising food prices and energy costs create for the poor and developing nations around the world.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because alternative fuels are useless if vehicles cannot use them, we must move quickly to flexible fuel vehicles; we cannot expect  necessary investments in alternative fuels if this flexibility does not become standard.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must also produce more vehicles that operate on electricity and natural gas, both to reduce demand for oil and to cut CO2 emissions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Given that fully 97 percent of our current transportation vehicles rely on oil, we will aggressively support technological advances to reduce our petroleum dependence.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: For example, lightweight composites could halve the weight and double the gas mileage of cars and trucks, and together with flex-fuel and electric vehicles, could usher in a renaissance in the American auto industry.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: By increasing our American energy supply and decreasing the long term demand for oil, we will be well positioned to address the challenge of climate change and continue our longstanding responsibility for stewardship over the environment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The same human economic activity that has brought freedom and opportunity to billions has also increased the amount of carbon in the atmosphere.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: While the scope and longterm consequences of this are the subject of ongoing scientific research, common sense dictates that the United States should take measured and reasonable steps today to reduce any impact on the environment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Those steps, if consistent with our global competitiveness will also be good for our national security, our energy independence, and our economy.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Any policies should be global in nature, based on sound science and technology, and should not harm the economy.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As part of a global climate change strategy, Republicans support technology-driven, market-based solutions that will decrease emissions, reduce excess greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere, increase energy efficiency, mitigate the impact of climate change where it occurs, and maximize any ancillary benefits climate change might offer for the economy.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To reduce emissions in the short run, we will rely upon the power of new technologies, as dis cussed above, especially zero-emission energy sources such as nuclear and other alternate power sources.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: But innovation must not be hamstrung by Washington bickering, regulatory briar patches, or obstructionist law suits.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Empowering Washington will only lead to unintended consequences and unimagined economic and environmental pain; instead, we must unleash the power of scientific know how and competitive markets.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because the issue of climate change is global, it must become a truly global concern as well.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: All developed and developing economies, particularly India and China, can make significant contributions in dealing with the matter.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It would be unrealistic and counterproductive to expect the U.S. to carry burdens which are more appropriately shared by all.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because Republicans believe that solutions to the risk of global climate change will be found in the ingenuity of the American people, we propose a Climate Prize for scientists who solve the challenges of climate change.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Honoraria of many millions of dollars would be a small price for technological developments that eliminate our need for gas-powered cars or abate atmospheric carbon.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans caution against the doomsday climate change scenarios peddled by the aficionados of centralized command-and-control government.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We can — and should — address the risk of climate change based on sound science without succumbing to the no-growth radicalism that treats climate questions as dogma rather than as situations to be managed responsibly.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: A robust economy will be essential to dealing with the risk of climate change, and we will insist on reasonable policies that do not force Americans to sacrifice their way of life or trim their hopes and dreams for their children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This perspective serves not only the people of the United States but also the world's poorest peoples, who would suffer terribly if climate change is severe — just as they would if the world economy itself were to be crippled.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must not allow either outcome.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Republican perspective on the environment is in keeping with our longstanding appreciation for nature and gratitude for the bounty the Almighty has bestowed upon the American people.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It was Republican President Theodore Roosevelt who said, "The conservation of natural resources is the fundamental problem.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Unless we solve that problem, it will avail us little to solve all others."
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We agree.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Whether through family vacations, hunting or fishing trips, backpacking excursions, or weekend hikes, Americans of all backgrounds share a commitment to protecting the environment and the opportunities it offers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In addition, the public should have access to public lands for recreational activities such as hunting, hiking, and fishing.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In caring for the land and water, private ownership has been the best guarantee of conscientious stewardship, while the world's worst instances of environmental degradation have occurred under governmental control.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: By the same token, it is no accident that the most economically advanced countries also have the strongest environmental protections.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our national progress toward cleaner air and water has been a major accomplishment of the American people.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: By balancing environmental goals with economic growth and job creation, our diverse economy has made possible the investment needed to safeguard natural resources, protect endangered species, and create healthier living conditions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: State and local initiatives to clean up contaminated sites — brownfields — have exceeded efforts directed by Washington.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: That progress can continue if grounded in sound science, long-term planning, and a multiuse approach to resources.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Government at all levels should protect private property rights by cooperating with landowners' efforts and providing incentives to protect fragile environments, endangered species, and maintain the natural beauty of America.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republican leadership has led to the rejuvenation and renewal of our National Park system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Future expansion of that system, as well as designation of National Wilderness areas or Historic Districts, should be undertaken only with the active participation and consent of relevant state and local governments and private property owners.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Americans have the best doctors, the best hospitals, the most innovative medical technology, and the best scientists in the world.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our challenge and opportunity is to build around them the best health care system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans believe the key to real reform is to give control of the health care system to patients and their health care providers, not bureaucrats in government or business.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: There are reasons why American families and businesses are dissatisfied with the current state of health care: * Most Americans work longer and harder to pay for health care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Dedicated health care providers are changing careers to avoid litigation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * The need to hold onto health insurance is driving family decisions about where to live and work.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Many new parents worry about the loss of coverage if they choose to stay at home with their children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * The need — and the bills — for long-term care are challenging families and government alike.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * American businesses are becoming less competitive in the global marketplace because of insurance costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Some federal programs with no benefit to patients have grown exponentially, adding layers of bureaucracy between patients and their care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It is not enough to offer only increased access to a system that costs too much and does not work for millions of Americans.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Republican goal is more ambitious: Better health care for lower cost.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: How do we ensure that all Americans have the peace of mind that comes from owning high-quality, comprehensive health coverage?
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The first rule of public policy is the same as with medicine: Do no harm.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The American people rejected Democrats~ attempted government takeover of health care in 1993, and they remain skeptical of politicians who would send us down that road.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans support the private practice of medicine and oppose socialized medicine in the form of a government-run universal health care system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans pledge that as we reform our health care system: * We will protect citizens against any and all   risky restructuring efforts that would complicate or ration health care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will encourage health promotion and disease prevention.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will facilitate cooperation, not confrontation, among patients, providers, payers, and all stakeholders in the health care system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will not put government between patients and their health care providers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will not put the system on a path that empowers Washington bureaucrats at the expense of patients.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will not raise taxes instead of reducing health care costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We will not replace the current system with the staggering inefficiency, maddening irrationality, and uncontrollable costs of a government monopoly.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Radical restructuring of health care would be unwise.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We want all Americans to be able to choose the best health care provider, hospital, and health coverage for their needs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We believe that real reform is about improving your access to a health care provider, your control over care, and your ability to afford that care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We will continue to advocate for simplification of the system and the empowerment of patients.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This is in stark contrast to the other party's insistence on putting Washington in charge of patient care, which has blocked any progress on meeting these goals.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We offer a detailed program that will improve the quality, cost, and coverage of health care throughout the nation, and we will turn that plan into reality.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans believe all Americans should be able to obtain an affordable health care plan, including a health savings account, which meets their needs and the needs of their families.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Families and health care providers are the key to real reform, not lawyers and bureaucrats.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To empower families, we must make insurance more affordable and more secure, and give employees the option of owning coverage that is not tied to their job.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Patients should not have to worry about losing their insurance.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Insurance companies should have to worry about losing patients’ business.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The current tax system discriminates against individuals who do not receive health care from their employers, gives more generous health tax benefits to upper income employees, and fails to provide every American with the ability to purchase an affordable health care plan.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans propose to correct inequities in the current tax code that drive up the number of uninsured and to level the playing field so that individuals who choose a health insurance plan in the individual market face no tax penalty.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: All Americans should receive the same tax benefit as those who are insured through work, whether through a tax credit or other means.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Individuals with pre-existing conditions must be protected; we will help these individuals by building on the experiences of innovative states rather than by creating a new unmanageable federal entitlement.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We strongly urge that managed care organizations use the practice patterns and medical treatment guidelines from the state in which the patient lives when making medical coverage decisions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because the family is our basic unit of society, we fully support parental rights to consent to medical treatment for their children including mental health treatment, drug treatment, alcohol treatment, and treatment involving pregnancy, contraceptives and abortion.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: While delivering control of health coverage to families and individuals, Republicans will also advance a variety of targeted reforms to improve the quality of care, lower costs, and help Americans — men, women, and children — live longer and healthier lives.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Chronic diseases — in many cases, preventable conditions — are driving health care costs, consuming three of every four health care dollars.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We can reduce demand for medical care by fostering personal responsibility within a culture of wellness, while increasing access to preventive services, including improved nutrition and breakthrough medications that keep people healthy and out of the hospital.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To reduce the incidence of diabetes, cancer, heart disease, and stroke, we call for a national grassroots campaign against obesity, especially among children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for continuation of efforts to decrease use of tobacco, especially among the young.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: A culture of wellness needs to include the treatment of mental health conditions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We believe all Americans should have access to affordable, quality health care, including individuals struggling with mental illness.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: For this reason, we believe it is important that mental health care be treated equally with physical health care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Clear information about health care empowers patients.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It lets consumers make better decisions about where to spend their health care dollars, thereby fostering competition and lowering costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Patients must have information to make sound decisions about their health care providers, hospitals, and insurance companies.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Advances in medical technology are revolutionizing medicine.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Information technology is key to early detection and treatment of chronic disease as well as fetal care and health care in rural areas — especially where our growing wireless communications network is available.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The simple step of modernizing recordkeeping will mean faster, more accurate treatment, fewer medical errors, and lower costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Closing the health care information gap can reduce both under-utilization (the diabetic who forgets to refill an insulin prescription) and over-utilization (the patient who endures repetitive tests because providers have not shared test results).
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Every patient must have access to legal remedies for malpractice, but meritless lawsuits drive up insurance rates to outrageous levels and ultimately drive up the number of uninsured.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Frivolous lawsuits also drive up the cost of health care as health care providers are forced to practice defensive medicine, such as ordering unnecessary tests.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Many leave their practices rather than deal with the current system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This emergency demands medical liability reform.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Patients deserve access to health care providers they trust who will personalize and coordinate their care to ensure they receive the right treatment with the right health care provider at the right time.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Providers should be paid for keeping people well, not for the number of tests they run or procedures they perform.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The current cookie-cutter system of reimbursement needs restructuring from the view of the patient, not the accountant or Washington bureaucrat.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: A state-regulated national market for health insurance means more competition, more choice, and lower costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Families — as well as fraternal societies, churches and community groups, and small employers — should be able to purchase policies across state lines.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The best practices and lowest prices should be available in every state.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call upon state legislators to carefully consider the cost of medical mandates, and we salute those Republican governors who are leading the way in demonstrating ways to provide affordable health care options.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The financial burdens and emotional challenges of ensuring adequate care for elderly family members affect every American, especially with today's aging population.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must develop new ways to support individuals, not just institutions, so that older Americans can have a real choice whether to stay in their homes.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This is true not only with regard to Medicaid, where we spend $100 billion annually on long-term care, but also for those who do not qualify for that assistance.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We believe in the importance of primary care specialties and supporting the physician's role in the evaluation and management of disease.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We also encourage practice in rural and underserved areas of America.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support federal investment in basic and applied biomedical research.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This commitment will maintain America's global competitiveness, advance innovative science that can lead to medical breakthroughs, and turn the tide against diseases affecting millions of Americans — diseases that account for the majority of our health care costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The United States leads in this research, as evidenced by our growing biotechnology industry, but foreign competition is increasing.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: One way government can help preserve the promise of American innovation is to ensure that our intellectual property laws remain robust.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Federal research dollars should be spent as though lives are at stake — because, in fact, they are.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Research protocols must consider the special needs of formerly neglected groups if we are to make significant progress against breast and prostate cancer, diabetes, and other killers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Taxpayer-funded medical research must be based on sound science, with a focus on both prevention and treatment, and in accordance with the humane ethics of the Hippocratic Oath.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In that regard, we call for a major expansion of support for the stem-cell research that now shows amazing promise and offers the greatest hope for scores of diseases — with adult stem cells, umbilical cord blood, and cells reprogrammed into pluripotent stem cells — without the destruction of embryonic human life.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for a ban on human cloning and a ban on the creation of or experimentation on human embryos for research purposes.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We believe medicines and treatments should be designed to prolong and enhance life, not destroy it.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Therefore, federal funds should not be used for drugs that cause the destruction of human life.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Furthermore, the Drug Enforcement Administration ban on use of controlled substances for physician-assisted suicide should be restored.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The health care profession can be both a profession and a calling.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: No health care professional — doctor, nurse, or pharmacist — or organization should ever be required to perform, provide for, or refer for a health care service against their conscience for any reason.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This is especially true of the religious organizations which deliver a major portion of America’s health care, a service rooted in the charity of faith communities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the provision of quality and accessible health care options for our nation’s seniors and disabled individuals and recognize that in order to meet this goal we must confront the special challenges posed by the growth of Medicare costs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Its projected growth is out of control and threatens to squeeze out other programs, while funding constraints lead to restricted access to treatment for many seniors.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: There are solutions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Medicare can be a leader for the rest of our health care system by encouraging treatment of the whole patient.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Specifically, we should compensate doctors who coordinate care, especially for those with multiple chronic conditions, and eliminate waste and inefficiency.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Medicare patients must have more control of their care and choice regarding their doctors, and the benefits of competition must be delivered to the patients themselves if Medicare is to provide quality health care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: And Medicare patients must be free to add their own funds, if they choose, to any government benefits, to be assured of unrationed care.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Finally, because it is isolated from the free market forces that encourage innovation, competition, affordability, and expansion of options, Medicare is especially susceptible to fraud and abuse.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The program loses tens of billions of dollars annually in erroneous and fraudulent payments.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We are determined to root out the fraud and eliminate this assault on the taxpayer.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our Medicaid obligations will consume $5 trillion over the next ten years.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Medicaid now accounts for 20-25 percent of state budgets and threatens to overwhelm state governments for the indefinite future.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We can do better while spending less
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: . A first step is to give Medicaid ~ recipients more health care options.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Several states have allowed beneficiaries to buy regular health insurance with their Medicaid dollars.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This removes the Medicaid "stamp" from people’s foreheads, provides beneficiaries with better access to doctors, and saves taxpayers~ money.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must ensure that taxpayer money is focused on caring for U.S. citizens and other individuals in our country legally.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To protect the American people from the threats we face in the century ahead, we must develop and stockpile medicines and vaccines so we can deliver them where urgently needed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our health care infrastructure must have the surge capacity to handle large numbers of patients in times of crisis, whether it is a repeat of Hurricane Katrina, a flu pandemic, or a bioterror attack on multiple cities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans will ensure that this infrastructure, including the needed communications capacity, is closely integrated into our homeland security needs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Education is a parental right, a state and local responsibility, and a national strategic interest.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Maintaining America's pre-eminence requires a world-class system of education, with high standards, in which all students can reach their potential.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: That requires considerable improvement over our current 70 percent high school graduation rate and six-year graduation rate of only 57 percent for colleges.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Education is essential to competitiveness, but it is more than just training for the work force of the future.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It is through education that we ensure the transmission of a culture, a set of values we hold in common.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It has prepared generations for responsible citizenship in a free society, and it must continue to do so.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our party is committed to restoring the civic mission of schools envisioned by the founders of the American public school system.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Civic education, both in the classroom and through service learning, should be a cornerstone of American public education and should be central to future school reform efforts.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: All children should have access to an excellent education that empowers them to secure their own   freedom and contribute to the betterment of our society.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We reaffirm the principles that have been the foundation of the nation’s educational progress toward that goal: accountability for student academic achievement; periodic testing on the fundamentals of learning, especially math and reading, history and geography; transparency, so parents and the general public know which schools best serve their students; and flexibility and freedom to innovate so schools and districts can best meet the needs of their students.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We advocate policies and methods that are proven and effective: building on the basics, especially phonics; ending social promotion; merit pay for good teachers; classroom discipline; parental involvement; and strong leadership by principals.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We reject a one-size-fits-all approach and support parental options, including home schooling, and local innovations such as schools or classes for boys only or for girls only and alternative and innovative school schedules.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We recognize and appreciate the importance of innovative education environments, particularly homeschooling, for stimulating academic achievement.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose over-reaching judicial decisions which deny children access to such environments.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support state efforts to build coordination between elementary and secondary education  and higher education such as K-16 councils and dual credit programs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To ensure that all students will have access to the mainstream of American life, we support the English First approach and oppose divisive programs that limit students' future potential.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: All students must be literate in English, our common language, to participate in the promise of America.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The family is the most powerful influence on a child's ability to succeed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As such, parents are our children's first and foremost teachers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support family literacy, which improves the literacy, language, and life skills of both parents and children along with the continued improvement of early childhood programs, such as Head Start, from low-income families.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We reaffirm our support for the child care tax credit that helps parents choose the care best for their family.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: For students to meet world class standards, they must have access to world class teachers, whether in person or through virtual public schools that can bring high-quality instruction into the classroom.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: School districts must have the authority to recruit, reward, and retain the best and brightest teachers, and principals must have the authority to select and assign teachers without regard to collective bargaining agreements.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because qualified teachers are often not available through traditional routes, we support local efforts to create an adjunct teacher corps of experts from higher education, business, and the military to fill in when needed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Teachers must be protected against frivolous litigation and should be able to take reasonable actions   to maintain discipline and order in the classroom.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We encourage the private-public partnerships and mentoring that can make classroom time more meaningful to students by integrating it with learning beyond school walls.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: These efforts are crucial to lowering the drop-out rate and helping at-risk students realize their potential.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We encourage state efforts to ensure that personnel who interact with children pass thorough background checks and are held to the highest standards of conduct.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Partnerships between schools and businesses can be especially important in STEM subjects: science, technology, engineering and math.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The need to improve secondary education in those fields can be measured by the number of remedial courses now offered at the college level.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our country's reliance upon foreign talent in those areas begins with insufficient emphasis upon them in the high school years.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We applaud those who are changing that situation by giving young people real-world experience in the private sector and by providing students with rigorous technical and academic courses that give students the skills and knowledge necessary to be productive members in a competitive American workforce.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Parents should be able to decide the learning environment that is best for their child.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support choice in education for all families, especially those with children trapped in dangerous and failing schools, whether through charter schools, vouchers or tax credits for attending faith-based or other non-public schools, or the option of home schooling.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for the vigilant enforcement of laws designed to protect family rights and privacy in education.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We will energetically assert the right of students to engage in voluntary prayer in schools and to have equal access to school facilities for religious purposes.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We renew our call for replacing "family planning" programs for teens with increased funding for abstinence education, which teaches abstinence until marriage as the responsible and expected standard of behavior.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Abstinence from sexual activity is the only protection that is 100 percent effective against out-of wedlock pregnancies and sexually transmitted diseases, including HIV/AIDS when transmitted sexually.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose school-based clinics that provide referrals, counseling, and related services for abortion and contraception.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Schools should not ask children to answer offensive or intrusive personal non-academic questionnaires without parental consent. It is not the role of the teacher or school administration to recommend or require the use of psychotropic medications that must be prescribed by a physician.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Although the Constitution assigns the federal government no role in local education, Washington's authority over the nation's schools has increased dramatically.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In less than a decade, annual federal funding has shot up 41 percent to almost $25 billion, while the regulatory burden on state and local governments has risen by about 6.7 million hours — and added $141 million in costs — during that time.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for a review of Department of Education programs and administration to identify and eliminate ineffective programs, to respect the role of states, and to better meet state needs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To get our schools back to the basics of learning, we support initiatives to block-grant more Department of Education funding to the states, with requirements for state-level standards, assessments, and public reporting to ensure transparency.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Local educators must be free to end ineffective programs and reallocate resources where they are most needed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because a federal mandate on the states must include the promised federal funding, we will fulfill the promise of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act to cover 40 percent of the costs incurred because of that legislation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We urge preventive efforts in early childhood, especially assistance in gaining pre-reading skills, to help many youngsters move beyond the need for IDEA’s protections.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our country's system of higher education — public and private, secular and religious, large and small institutions — is unique for its excellence, its diversity, and its accessibility.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Learning is a safeguard of liberty.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Post-secondary education not only increases the earnings of individuals but advances economic development.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our colleges and universities drive much of the research that keeps America competitive.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must ensure that our higher education system meet the needs of the 21st century student and economy and remain innovative and accessible.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Students and their parents face formidable challenges in planning for college as costs continue to outpace inflation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Higher education seems immune from market controls and the law of supply and demand.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We commend those institutions which are directing a greater proportion of their endowment revenues toward tuition relief.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Republican vision for expanding access to higher education has led to two major advances, Education Savings Accounts and Section 529 accounts, by which millions of families now save for college.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: While federal student loans and grants have opened doors to learning for untold numbers of low-and middle-income students, the overall financial aid system, with its daunting forms and confused rationales, is nothing less than Byzantine.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It must be simplified.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for a presidential commission to undertake that task and to review the role of government regulations and policies in the tuition spiral.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We affirm our support for the public-private partnership that now offers students and their families a vibrant marketplace in selecting their student loan provider.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The challenge to American higher education is to make sure students can access education in whatever forms they want.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As mobility increases in all aspects of American life, student mobility, from school to school and from campus to campus, will require new approaches to admissions, evaluations, and credentialing.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Distance learning propelled by an expanding telecommunications sector and especially broadband, is certain to grow in importance — whether through public or private institutions — and federal law should not discriminate against the latter.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Lifelong learning will continue to transform the demographics of higher education, bringing older students and real-world experience to campus.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Community colleges are central to the future of higher education, especially as they build bridges between the world of work and the classroom.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Many of our returning veterans find community colleges to be welcoming environments where they can develop specific skills for use in the civilian workforce.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As the first responders to economic development and retraining of workers, these schools fulfill our national commitment of an affordable and readily accessible education for all.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Free speech on college campuses is to be celebrated, but there should be no place in academia for anti-Semitism or racism of any kind.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose the hiring, firing, tenure, and promotion practices at universities that discriminate on the basis of political or ideological belief.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: When federal taxes are used to support such practices, it is inexcusable.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We affirm the right of students and faculty to express their views in the face of the leftist dogmatism that dominates many institutions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To preserve the integrity and independence of the nation` s colleges, we will continue to ensure alternatives to ideological accrediting systems.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because some of the nation’s leading universities create or tolerate a hostile atmosphere toward the ROTC, we will rigorously enforce the provision of law, unanimously upheld by the Supreme Court, which denies those institutions federal research grants unless their military students have the full rights and privileges of other students.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: That must include the right to engage in ROTC activities on their own campus, rather than being segregated elsewhere.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans remain the party of vigorous action against crime and the party that empowers the law-abiding by protecting their right to keep and bear arms for self-protection.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our national experience over the past twenty years has shown that vigilance, tough yet fair prosecutors, meaningful sentences, protection of victims' rights, and limits on judicial discretion protect the innocent by keeping criminals off the streets.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Internet must be made safe for children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: That's why Republicans have led efforts to increase the funding necessary to track down and jail online predators through the Adam Walsh Act.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We commit to do whatever it takes, using all the tools of innovative technology, to thwart those who would prey upon our children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call on service providers to exercise due care to ensure that the Internet cannot become a safe haven for criminals.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Child pornography is a hideous form of child abuse.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Those who produce it — and those who   traffic in it — must be punished to the maximum extent of the law.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because it is an international problem, the Executive branch must carry the fight overseas to where the molesters perpetrate their evil.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Congress should expand the range of companies required to report the existence of child pornography, and we congratulate the social networking sites that agree to bar known sex offenders from participation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Millions of Americans suffer from problem or pathological gambling that can destroy families.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the law prohibiting gambling over the Internet.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Gang violence is a growing problem, not only in urban areas but in many suburbs and rural communities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It has escalated with the rise of gangs composed largely of illegal aliens, most of whose victims are law-abiding members of immigrant communities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for stronger enforcement and deter mined prosecution of gang conspiracies.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Illegal allien gang members must be removed from the United States immediately upon arrest or after the completion of any sentence imposed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Aliens convicted of crimes that render them removable from the United States must be removed as soon as possible after the completion of their sentences through the immediate transfer of their custody to Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Criminals behind bars cannot harm the general public. To that end: * We support mandatory sentencing provisions for gang conspiracy crimes, violent or sexual offenses against children, rape, and assaults resulting in serious bodily injury.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Gang rape, child rape, and rape committed in the course of another felony deserve, at the least, mandatory life imprisonment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We oppose the granting of parole to dangerous or repeat felons.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * Courts must have the option of imposing the death penalty in capital murder cases and other instances of heinous crime, while federal review of those sentences should be streamlined to focus on claims of innocence and to prevent delaying tactics by defense attorneys.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: * We encourage the use of advanced technology to monitor nonviolent criminals.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Public authorities at all levels must cooperate to regain control of the nation’s correctional institutions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It is unacceptable that prison officers should live in fear of the inmates they guard.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Similarly, persons jailed for whatever cause should be protected against cruel or degrading treatment by other   inmates.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We cannot allow correctional facilities to become ethnic or racial battlegrounds.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Breaking the cycle of crime begins with the children of those who are incarcerated.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Deprived of a parent through no fault of their own, these youngsters should be a special concern of our schools, social services, and religious institutions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Government at all levels should work with faith-based institutions that have proven track records in diverting young and first offenders from criminal careers through Second Chance and similar programs.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Individuals, including juveniles, who are repeat offenders or who commit serious crimes need to be prosecuted and punished.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In solidarity with those who protect us, we call for mandatory prison time for all assaults involving bodily injury to law enforcement officers.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Reviews of death sentences imposed for murdering a police officer should be expedited, and a retrial of the penalty phase of the killer's trial should be allowed in the absence of a unanimous verdict.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the right of off-duty and retired officers to carry firearms.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Criminals should be barred from seeking monetary damages for injuries they incur while committing a crime.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In recent years, many federal resources for law enforcement have been shifted to the fight against terror.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To compensate for that loss of manpower — and with the significant increase in cybercrime, identity theft, and human trafficking — several thousand new FBI agents, U.S. marshals, immigration officers, and Border Patrol agents are needed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The human toll of drug addiction and abuse hits all segments of American society.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It is an international problem as well, with most of the narcotics in this country coming from beyond our borders.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We will continue the fight against producers, traffickers, and distributors of illegal substances through the collaboration of state, federal, and local law enforcement.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the work of those who help individuals struggling with addiction, and we support strengthening drug education and prevention programs to avoid addiction.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We endorse state and local initiatives, such as Drug Courts, that are trying new approaches to curbing drug abuse and diverting first-time offenders to rehabilitation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Twenty-six years ago, President Reagan~ s Task Force on Victims of Crime, calling the neglect of crime victims a national disgrace, proposed a constitutional amendment to secure their formal rights.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Today, that disgrace persists in courtrooms across the nation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Innocent victims — battered women, abused children, the loved ones of the murdered — still may not be told when their case is being heard.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: They can be excluded from the courtroom even when the defendant and his friends may be present.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: They have no right to a speedy trial, and a judge or parole board has no obligation to consider their personal safety in making release decisions.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In short, the innocent have far fewer rights than the accused.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call   on Congress to correct this imbalance by sending to the states for ratification a constitutional amendment to protect the rights of crime victims.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In addition, crime victims should be assured of access to legal and social services, and the Crime Victims Fund established under President Reagan should be used solely for that purpose.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because our Constitution is based on the principles of individual liberty and limited government, we must always ensure that law enforcement respects the civil and constitutional rights of the people.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: While we wage war on terrorism in foreign lands, it is sometimes necessary for intelligence agencies and law enforcement officials to pursue terrorist threats at home.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: However, no expansion of governmental powers should occur at the expense of our constitutional liberties.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The two most effective forces in reducing crime and other social ills are strong families and caring communities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Both reinforce constructive conduct and ethical standards by setting examples and providing safe havens from dangerous and destructive behaviors.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Given the weight of social science evidence concerning the crucial role played by the traditional family in setting a child's future course, we urge a thoughtful review of governmental policies and programs to ensure that  they do not undermine that institution.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Decentralized decision-making in the place of official controls empowers individuals and groups to tackle social problems in partnership with government.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Bureaucracy is no longer a credible approach to helping those in need.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: This is especially true in light of alternatives such as faith-based organizations, which tend to have a greater degree of success than others in dealing with problems such as substance abuse and domestic violence.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: To accomplish their missions, those groups must be able to rely upon people who share their faith; their hiring must not be subjected to government regulation and mandates.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: From its founding, America has been an idea as much as a political or geographic entity.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: It has meant, for untold millions around the world, a set of ideals that speak to the highest aspirations of humanity.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: From its own beginning, the Republican Party has boldly asserted those ideals, as we now do again, to affirm the rights of the people under the rule of law.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We uphold the right of individual Americans to own firearms, a right which antedated the Constitution and was solemnly confirmed by the Second Amendment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We applaud the Supreme Court's decision in Heller affirming that right, and we assert the individual responsibility to safely use and store firearms.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call on the next president to appoint judges who will similarly respect the Constitution.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Gun ownership is responsible citizenship, enabling Americans to defend themselves, their property, and communities.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We call for education in constitutional rights in schools, and we support the option of firearms training in federal programs serving senior citizens and women.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We urge immediate action to review the automatic denial of gun ownership to returning   members of the Armed Forces who have suffered trauma during service to their country.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We condemn frivolous lawsuits against firearms manufacturers, which are transparent attempts to deprive citizens of their rights.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose federal licensing of law-abiding gun owners and national gun registration as violations of the Second Amendment.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We recognize that gun control only affects and penalizes law-abiding citizens, and that such proposals are ineffective at reducing violent crime.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Individual rights — and the responsibilities that go with them — are the foundation of a free society.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: From the time of Lincoln, equality of individuals has been a corner stone of the Republican Party.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our commitment to equal opportunity extends from landmark school-choice legislation for the students of Washington D.C. to historic appointments at the highest levels of government.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We consider discrimination based on sex, race, age, religion, creed, disability, or national origin to be immoral, and we will strongly enforce anti-discrimination statutes.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We ask all to join us in rejecting the forces of hatred and bigotry and in denouncing all who practice or promote racism, anti-Semitism, ethnic prejudice, or religious intolerance.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As a matter of principle, Republicans oppose any attempts to create race-based governments within the United States, as well as any domestic governments not bound by the Constitution or the Bill of Rights.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Precisely because we oppose discrimination, we reject preferences, quotas, and set-asides, whether in education or in corporate boardrooms.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The government should not make contracts on this basis, and neither should corporations.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support efforts to help low-income individuals get a fair shot based on their potential and merit, and we affirm the commonsense approach of the Chief Justice of the United States: that the way to stop discriminating on the basis of race is to stop discriminating.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The symbol of our unity, to which we all pledge allegiance, is the flag.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: By whatever legislative method is most feasible, Old Glory should be given legal protection against desecration.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We condemn decisions by activist judges to deny children the opportunity to say the Pledge of Allegiance in public school.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support freedom of speech and freedom of the press and oppose attempts to violate or weaken those rights, such as reinstatement of the so-called Fairness Doctrine.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Faithful to the first guarantee of the Declaration of Independence, we assert the inherent dignity and sanctity of all human life and affirm that the unborn   child has a fundamental individual right to life which cannot be infringed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support a human life amendment to the Constitution, and we endorse legislation to make clear that the Fourteenth Amendment's protections apply to unborn children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We oppose using public revenues to promote or perform abortion and will not fund organizations which advocate it.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the appointment of judges who respect traditional family values and the sanctity and dignity of innocent human life.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We have made progress.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The Supreme Court has upheld prohibitions against the barbaric practice of partial-birth abortion.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: States are now permitted to extend health-care coverage to children before birth.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: And the Born Alive Infants Protection Act has become law; this law ensures that infants who are born alive during an abortion receive all treatment and care that is provided to all newborn infants and are not neglected and left to die.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We must protect girls from exploitation and statutory rape through a parental notification requirement.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We all have a moral obligation to assist, not to penalize, women struggling with the challenges of an unplanned pregnancy.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: At its core, abortion is a fundamental assault on the sanctity of innocent human life.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Women deserve better than abortion.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Every effort should be made to work with women considering abortion to enable and empower them to choose life.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We salute those who provide them alternatives, including pregnancy care centers, and we take pride in the tremendous increase in adoptions that has followed Republican legislative initiatives.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Respect for life requires efforts to include persons with disabilities in education, employment, the justice system, and civic participation.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In keeping with that commitment, we oppose the non-consensual withholding of care or treatment from  people with disabilities, as well as the elderly and infirm, just as we oppose euthanasia and assisted suicide, which endanger especially those on the margins of society.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because government should set a positive standard in hiring and contracting for the services of persons with disabilities, we need to update the statutory authority for the Ability One program, the main avenue by which those productive members of our society can offer high quality services at the best possible value.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Because our children's future is best preserved within the traditional understanding of marriage, we call for a constitutional amendment that fully protects marriage as a union of a man and a woman, so that judges cannot make other arrangements equivalent to it.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: In the absence of a national amendment, we support the right of the people of the various states to affirm traditional marriage through state initiatives.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans recognize the importance of having in the home a father and a mother who are married.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The two-parent family still provides the best environment of stability, discipline, responsibility, and character.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Children in homes without fathers are more likely to commit a crime, drop out of school, become violent, become teen parents, use illegal drugs, become mired in poverty, or have emotional or behavioral problems.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We support the courageous efforts of single-parent families to provide a stable home for their children.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Children are our nation’s most precious resource.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We also salute and support the efforts of foster and adoptive families.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Republicans have been at the forefront of protecting traditional marriage laws, both in the states and in Congress.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: A Republican Congress enacted the Defense of Marriage Act, affirming the right of states not to recognize same-sex "marriages' licensed in other states.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Unbelievably, the Democratic Party has now pledged to repeal the Defense of Marriage Act, which would subject every state to the redefinition of marriage by a judge without ever allowing the people to vote on the matter.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We also urge Congress to use its Article III, Section 2 power to prevent activist federal judges from imposing upon the rest of the nation the judicial activism in Massachusetts and California.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: We also encourage states to review their marriage and divorce laws in order to strengthen marriage.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: As the family is our basic unit of society, we oppose initiatives to erode parental rights.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: Our Constitution guarantees the free exercise of religion and forbids any religious test for public office, and it likewise prohibits the establishment of a state-sponsored creed.
title: 2008 Republican Platform

text: The balance between those two ideals has been distorted by judicial rulings which attempt to drive faith out of the public arena.
title: 2008 Republican Platform
